The Floor Queue Only the familiar runs builds and tests on this box, one heavy run at a time (operator, 2026-11-25, after the second WSL VHD crash). The queue the familiar drains stands as one append log, `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/state/test-floor`: `QUEUE` enters a tasked spirit's hand-back, `RUN` and `WHY` carry its ticket body, `TAKE` marks the floor held, `DONE` lands the bench gate's verdict with its byte rows (`wrote=`, `c-drop=`), `DROP` sets a ticket down unrun. `[[<ledger>]floor-queue[<view>],[<arg>]]` answers each view: waiting, next, skip, taken, green, red, stopped, dropped, budget, ticket, runs, sha, green-sha. <<~/ahu>> <<~ ahu slot=`#/law`>> !! The Queue Law Runs In The Wiki The placement law (mandate/floor-gate-1): code that CAN live in the wiki VM MUST. The fold (`packages/lararium-tw5/src/floor-ledger.ts`) orders tickets by their place in the log, never by a clock; a QUEUE over a waiting ticket folds to nothing, and a waiting ticket whose sha already holds a GREEN verdict reads `skip`. The host tools (`tools/floor-ledger.mjs`, `tools/floor-run.mjs`) append lines through the tiddler door and ask through the render door; while the doors stand dark they append to the flat mirror `<passwd home>/.lares-scratch/.floor/queue.log`, and `node tools/floor-ledger.mjs otakiage` folds it back in. The host gates (the one flock, the floor-guard hook, the C: sampler, source-only benches, the docker build lock) stay in `tools/`, because they gate host processes. <<~/ahu>> <<~ ahu slot=`#/callers`>> !! Callers The floor page (`lar:///ha.ka.ba/lararium/tw5/floor/page`) renders the views; `tools/floor-run.mjs --ticket <id>` asks `skip` before it runs, and `tools/floor-ledger.mjs ask <view> [<arg>]` asks any view. <<~/ahu>> <<~ ahu slot=`#/caps-cost`>> !! Caps and Cost The operator reads through the wiki it runs in and writes nothing; one call folds the ledger once. <<~/ahu>> <<~ ahu slot=`#/source`>> !! The Fold A folded carrier reads as the meme file rests on disk (the declaration, the head, the meta, each slot's `ahu` pair) with a folded slot's body standing as its `has` line (bytes, first line) and the one command that fetches it. `[[<uri>]meme-fold[<open slots>],[<face>]]` folds any meme root, and answers a plain record as a carrier too: its fields ride the meta, a short text rides whole (a transclusion stays a transclusion, folded and renderable), a longer one folds to its `has` line and its read command. `[[<pet>]spirit-fold[<rank>],[<face>]]` folds a tasked spirit's shrine by aperture: every slot folded at pulse, the entry slot unfolded at beat, the attention and open slots at measure (arc reads the same), the whole carrier at theme; it names the pet's card and its render command where one stands, and answers a card with no shrine as a carrier. <<~/ahu>> <<~ ahu slot=`#/law`>> !! The Fold Runs In The Wiki The operators read the wiki's own records, recompose through the deserializer's recompose, cut at the decomposer's top-level slot scan, write each `has` line through the read gradient and re-stamp the block check through the frame writer (`packages/lararium-tw5/src/carrier-fold.ts`). So `lares meme check` passes on a fold, an unfolded slot rides byte for byte, and no door builds the grammar outside the engine. The rank an aperture names and every command a fold carries stand in the pure core `packages/lararium-mesh/src/spirit-unfold.ts`, bundled here and read by the host door for the one call it sends. One render serves a shrine, a card, a handback record and any message between streams of thought (the design rests on the memory stage at `lar:///ha.ka.ba/kahua/memory/reference/tasked-spirit`). <<~/ahu>> <<~ ahu slot=`#/callers`>> !! Callers The `<<spirit-unfold pet aperture face>>` macro (`lar:///ha.ka.ba/lararium/tw5/macros/spirit-unfold`) hands the engine one text node whose value `spirit-fold` answers, so the carrier rides out byte for byte. `lares spirit om <pet>` and `lares spirit hum <pet>` send the wiki's `wiki-render` verb that one macro call, by `--aperture`; `lares wiki render --recipe default --form text --text '<<spirit-unfold pet:"<pet>" aperture:"pulse">>'` reads the same fold; a browser tab calls the macro or either operator in any tiddler. The operators load over the grammar skin's deserializer, meme-ast and frame libraries, and never the other way. <<~/ahu>> <<~ ahu slot=`#/caps-cost`>> !!
